title: Linear Momentum
body:
**Linear momentum** is mass times velocity.

$$
\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v}
$$

It is a [[Vector]], pointing along the velocity, and it is conserved for any system with no
external force acting on it, whatever happens between the objects inside. Internal forces come
in third-law pairs by [[Newton's Laws]], so they cancel in the total.

```
2 kg at 3 m/s:    p = 6 kg·m/s to the right
```

Being a vector, momentum conservation holds separately in each direction, so a two-dimensional
collision gives two equations. Signs carry the direction in one dimension, and a sign error is
the most common failure in a collision problem.

Momentum and [[Kinetic Energy]] measure different things about the same motion, which is
why both are worth tracking. Momentum is linear in velocity and directional; kinetic energy is
quadratic and has no direction. Two objects of equal mass moving toward each other at the same
speed have zero total momentum and non-zero total energy, and that combination is exactly what
makes a head-on [[Collisions|collision]] destructive.

The second law is more generally stated as force equalling the rate of change of momentum,
which reduces to $F = ma$ when the mass is constant. [[Impulse]] is that statement integrated
over time.
